power_management_states.name: Active
power_management_states.description: Fully operational; node participates in the schedule and clock sync.

power_management_states.name: Ready
power_management_states.description: Configured and idle, awaiting a start command.

power_management_states.name: Sleep
power_management_states.description: Bus asleep; the node waits for a Wakeup Pattern (WUP) to wake.

power_management_states.name: Halt
power_management_states.description: Communication stopped; the CC has left the schedule.

fields.wakeup_mechanism: A node wakes a channel by transmitting a Wakeup Pattern (WUP), a configured number of Wakeup Symbols (WUS); the Bus Driver detects bus activity and wakes the host/CC. Wakeup is performed one channel at a time.

power_rails.purpose: Keeps wakeup detection alive while the bus sleeps.

fields.flexray_power_considerations: FlexRay defines a sleep/wakeup framework: the bus can sleep with the Bus Driver retaining wakeup-pattern detection, and a WUP wakes a channel before coldstart. Energy management is largely a transceiver (Bus Driver) and ECU concern; the protocol contributes the wakeup-symbol/pattern mechanism and the POC WAKEUP state.
fields.notes: FlexRay's protocol-level power intent is the wakeup/sleep mechanism (WUP/WUS detection by the Bus Driver, POC WAKEUP state) rather than a fine-grained power-domain spec. Detailed power rails and low-power transceiver behavior are defined by the electrical physical layer (ISO 17458-4) and the Bus Driver implementation.

extraction_hints: Look for power-domain partitioning, supply nets.
